questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: The most isolated places on Earth
Life in the Scottish Highlands
A survey showing who feels lonely and why
Why London is a crowded city
questions.why: Neil says loneliness is today's topic and the BBC has just completed a big survey about it.

questions.q: What does Sam think about being lonely in a crowd?
options: It's possible, because it's about feeling disconnected
It's impossible when there are so many people and things to do
It only happens to people from the countryside
It only happens to old people
questions.why: Sam says you can be lonely anywhere if you feel disconnected from the world around you.

questions.q: How seriously does the British government take loneliness?
options: It ignores the problem
It has a minister for loneliness
It pays people to visit the elderly
It did the survey itself
questions.why: Neil says the British government has a minister for loneliness.

questions.q: According to the research, which group feels lonely most often and most strongly?
options: People over 75
People living alone in the countryside
Parents with young children
People aged 16 to 24
questions.why: The report says people aged 16 to 24 experience loneliness more often and more intensely.

questions.q: How does Neil feel about this finding?
options: Surprised, because he expected older people
Not surprised at all
Worried about his own children
Doubtful that the survey is correct
questions.why: Neil says 'I was surprised by that' because he would have guessed older people.

questions.q: Why does Sam joke about Neil's home-cooked meals?
options: To say that Neil is a great cook
To suggest a stereotype is true in Neil's case
To invite Neil for dinner
To explain why Neil might feel lonely even in a busy city
questions.why: Sam says stereotypes may be true in some cases, 'I've eaten some of your home-cooked meals'.

questions.q: According to researchers at the University of Manchester, why might young people feel lonely?
options: They spend too much time online
They live a long way from their families and old friends
They are changing identity and learning to control emotions
They have fewer friends than older people
questions.why: They suggest it's a time of identity change, figuring out your place and learning to regulate emotions.

questions.q: What does the reporter mean by 'figuring out your place in the world'?
options: Choosing which country you would most like to live in
Finding a job near home
Learning to read maps
Understanding what to do with your life
questions.why: Neil explains that we are trying to understand the world and what to do with our lives.
